panels.title: Memory used
panels.description: Available memory includes reclaimable page cache, so MinIO and PostgreSQL file caching do not count as used.

panels.title: Disk busy (I/O utilisation)
panels.description: Near 100% means the disk is the bottleneck, whatever the CPU says.

panels.title: Root filesystem used
panels.description: Docker volumes of MinIO and PostgreSQL live on this filesystem. Success threshold: under 80%.

panels.title: Memory against its limit
panels.description: A container above its cap is OOM-killed; see the next panel.

panels.title: Heap used against max
panels.description: Uploads are read fully into memory (twice for images with thumbnails): watch this during the upload phase.

panels.title: GC time share
panels.description: Above about 10% the JVM spends its time collecting garbage instead of serving requests.

panels.title: Tomcat request threads
panels.description: Busy at max means requests queue. Slow uploads hold a thread for their whole duration.

panels.title: Buffer cache hit ratio
panels.description: Falls as the data outgrows shared_buffers and the OS cache; the data-growth phase should show it.

panels.title: Top statements by DB time
panels.description: Look the queryid up in pg_stat_statements to see the statement text.

panels.title: Stored data
panels.description: The cost per file for extrapolating to the six-month volume comes from this against the object count.

panels.title: CPU
panels.description: Logins hash passwords and are CPU-heavy; a registration burst shows up here first.

panels.title: Load generator (k6, pushed by remote write)
Response time (client side)
panels.description: Needs K6_PROMETHEUS_RW_TREND_STATS=p(95),p(99) on the k6 side. Success threshold: p95 under 500 ms.
